task_instance: Invoke pr-address-feedback on a pull request: gather all review comments/threads on the PR, order them coherently, present each feedback item with diff context and current code, and build an approvable resolution plan.
blocker_detail: The skill's entire deliverable is reading and triaging review feedback on a real pull request hosted on a GitHub service. Step 1 alone requires authenticated API/GraphQL calls (via the gh CLI) against a GitHub host to fetch review threads, review bodies, and conversation comments, plus git fetch of the PR head ref. No such pull request exists in this runtime, the PR host named in the skill is a placeholder standing for a resource I cannot reach, and completing it would require an authenticated GitHub account plus network access to that host. The safety rules forbid using credentials/tokens, account-bound services, and the github MCP/connector tools, and forbid writes to external services (the later steps post replies, resolve threads, push commits, and re-request reviewers). A PR with review comments is not sample input a user supplies locally; it lives on the hosted service, so it cannot be fabricated in the work directory without stubbing the service the skill depends on.
evidence: Read SKILL.md: skill fetches review threads with 'gh api graphql' (paginated), top-level reviews, and PR conversation comments, reading code from the PR head SHA via 'git fetch <base remote> refs/pull/<n>/head'; later carries out the plan with git push, gh api replies, resolveReviewThread GraphQL mutations, and re-request-reviewers POSTs. Verified tooling present but unusable for the task: 'gh version 2.89.0' and git at /usr/bin/git both exist, but the skill requires an authenticated GitHub account and a reachable GitHub host plus an actual PR, none of which are available or permitted under the safety rules. No deliverable (feedback index, per-item blocks, resolution plan) can be produced because there is no PR to read.
